sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.usage: The Peking government had contested institutions and rival military factions. Provincial governors largely controlled provincial troops and revenues. A Canton military government maintained a separate position. The report supports a composite political context, not a single warlord clique or uniform central authority.

sources.usage: The report distinguishes Nanking’s central government from powerful regional military authorities; Yen Hsi-shan controlled northern territory outside Manchuria. Suppression of revolts did not establish durable centralized control.
